title: Explain AI to others
desc: Prepare and give a clear talk that teaches AI to a younger audience
content_html:
What You'll Do

Leaders can explain technology clearly — and your own understanding actually grows when you have to teach it to someone else. If you can explain AI simply, in plain words, you really understand it. In this project you'll prepare and deliver a short, jargon-free explanation of AI aimed at a specific person, then improve it based on real feedback.

You'll Need

  • Paper and a pen for drafting
  • A timer
  • Optional: a simple scoring sheet (Clear? / No jargon? / Could they repeat it back?)

Steps

  1. Choose a specific audience — a parent, a younger sibling, or a head teacher.
  2. Write a three-sentence explanation of what AI is for that person, with no jargon.
  3. Say it out loud to a partner. Have them score it: Was it clear? Any jargon? Could they repeat it back in their own words?
  4. Rewrite your weakest sentence based on that feedback.
  5. Deliver your final version, and prove it worked by having your listener repeat the idea back.

Examples

  • Jargon-heavy (weak): "AI leverages neural architectures to perform inference on multimodal inputs."
  • Clear (strong): "AI is a computer that learns from lots of examples, so it can make good guesses about new things it has never seen before."

Tips

  • Ban yourself from five "jargon" words at the start (algorithm, neural network, model, data, inference) to force plain language.
  • The real test of understanding is your listener repeating it back — make that your score.
  • Short and clear beats long and impressive, every time.

Think About It

  • Why does teaching something to someone else deepen your own understanding?
  • How does your explanation change for a 6-year-old versus a head teacher?
  • What's one piece of jargon you used to use that you can now say in plain words?

Challenge Yourself

  • Easy: Turn your explanation into a one-page poster for a younger class.
  • Medium: Record a 60-second video explaining AI to a family member.
  • Hard: Plan and deliver a 5-minute mini-lesson that teaches a younger class one true thing about AI.
